limitations: The two historical uninstrumented 120 s winter recreation failures remain immutable and unexplained at an internal browser/GPU level; both later instrumented full-sequence runs passed.
Baseline clean phase assertions passed, but browser.close exceeded its separate 10000 ms cleanup deadline; do not describe its entire execution as an unqualified success.
Candidate full-sequence phases 386-396 are missing. Candidate second-generation factory and first-render durations are unavailable; only the observed combined interval is reported.

No successful end-of-run reconciliation of the in-page event list with JSONL was implemented. Binding rejection is ignored and all persisted numbered events arrived through console. No exact emission/transport/persistence loss cause is established.

Logging, delegated getters/setters and prototype wrappers alter timing. Four serial software-rendered observations do not establish a performance distribution, hardware FPS, or causal fix of the historical failures.

Baseline second-generation synchronous renderer.render was slow; this boundary cannot separate JS preparation, shader work, command submission, driver waits, previous work or readback-related effects. No GPU completion fence was inserted in these phase probes.

The correction eliminates demonstrated redundant backing setter writes. It preserves actual size/DPR updates and host static redraw behavior; it is not a renderer submission bound or scheduler correction.

No context-loss/error event was recorded in these streams; the candidate missing interval prevents a blanket complete-event claim. Later recorded context states are not lost and both full-sequence ready waits passed.
Final uninstrumented original suite, native input/visual evidence, two-cycle recreation regression and repository gates must be assessed separately.
